nodes.label: TARR ring labels use applied distance
nodes.rationale: Decided 2026-10-01 (Paul): TARR rings posted to DataSync are named '{percent}% - {miles}mi - {Category}' in a folder 'AZ LPB {Category} WiSAR' (Koester profiles use 'Koester LPB {Category} WiSAR'). Option A puts the distance the ring is actually drawn at into the label, after calibration. Miles come from each contour's threshold_m, WiSAR's cost-distance in metres, divided by 1609.344 and rounded to 2 decimals. Arizona with the Coconino checkbox off matches the table; with it on, multipliers are 1.05, 1.35, and 1.80. Unedited Koester uses category or global Coconino multipliers. Implemented by tarrCallsign() and ringNaming() in src/lib/wisarResults.ts.

nodes.label: TARR labels from table distance
nodes.rationale: Switch path if feedback wants labels to match the LPB table or Koester profile rather than the drawn ring. Rings themselves do not move. ringNaming() would read resolved.source_distances_km (pre-calibration kilometres) for the 25/50/75 band, falling back to threshold_m, and WisarTarrForm notes would say calibration moves the rings while labels keep the table values.

nodes.label: Coconino global calibration
nodes.rationale: Optional multipliers 1.05, 1.35, and 1.80 applied to Arizona TARR distances, and category or global multipliers for unedited Koester profiles. Under option A the DataSync label shows the calibrated miles.

nodes.label: Travel time rings and WiSAR export names
nodes.rationale: The applied-versus-table labeling decision does not change travel-time rings ('{n}h Travel Time' in WiSAR Distance Traveled), the map preview, downloads, or the GeoJSON/KML from WiSAR, which keep WiSAR's own '25% Percentile TARR' names and threshold remarks.
